questions.q: Why do crypto opportunities appear and vanish so quickly?
a: Blockchain transparency lets information spread extremely fast
Most crypto projects are run by a single secretive company
Regulators shut down new projects within days of launch
Investors are legally required to hold coins for a short time
questions.why: Lesson 1 explains that everything on the blockchain is public, so gaps get closed within about a day.

questions.q: What happened after users spotted a pricing error in Iron Finance?
a: A bank run sent both of its coins to zero within hours
The team fixed the error and the price doubled
Trading was paused for a year while auditors worked
The project was bought by one of the large crypto funds
questions.why: Lesson 1 uses the Iron Finance collapse as an example of how fast a new protocol can fail.

questions.q: What does Nat call the clearest sign that it is time to get out?
a: Believing you have figured out the game and are about to get rich
Losing a small amount of money on your very first trade
Reading too many explanations of blockchain terminology
Spending too little time in crypto chat groups
questions.why: Lesson 2 quotes Nat saying that feeling is the number one sign you have a problem.

questions.q: Why did Nat eventually step away from his crypto obsession?
a: Stress on his marriage made him reconsider what he valued
He lost all of his money in a single failed smart contract
He was banned from the platforms he used to trade
A large fund offered to buy his entire token holdings
questions.why: Lesson 3 says it took strain in his marriage for him to wake up and return to writing.

questions.q: What does Nat mean by getting good at the wrong thing?
a: Success at something you do not truly value can trap you
Practicing a skill for too long makes you worse at it
Only people with natural talent can succeed in crypto
Choosing the wrong teacher will ruin your career
questions.why: Lesson 3 explains that praise and money can keep you in a pursuit you will later regret.
